searchText: If we want to keep BLS validators slashable after the Q fork, we can delay withdrawability which I think should be enough. This will mean that we have 256 epochs of weak subjectivity after the fork with the decay proportional to the percentage of withdrawn BLS validators; i.e. 256 epochs after the fork those validators could attempt to finalize a conflicting checkpoint before the fork and avoid being slashed. Exiting validators via the queue will clog the queue and in case if < 2/3 switched to PQ the network will lose finality and start experience inactivity penalties. Compromising the length of WS period around the fork can be mitigated by announcing that explicitly and asking to carefully select the checkpoint when checkpoint-syncing right after the fork. Just pushed this commit (https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/commit/16c9b6a1357942dccbf5f50c561098cb9d32b2d7) which will immediately exit unregistered validators at the PQ fork but their withdrawal delay is 8192 epochs (~36 days). we can even consider longer than ~36 days. Question is that enough time to credibly social slash someone. This needs ACD governance, and client releases and even some testing Yep I see ~36 days as a minimum. I imagine it would take at least... * a week to decide to socially slash someone, * a couple days for clients to make releases with the change, * a week for testing and devnets, * a week for the network to update their nodes. a week for the network to update their nodes. this should be > 2 weeks imo, with annoucement and stuff. So maybe 45 days is better or even longer. excerpts.content:
If we want to keep BLS validators slashable after the Q fork, we can delay withdrawability which I think should be enough. This will mean that we have 256 epochs of weak subjectivity after the fork with the decay proportional to the percentage of withdrawn BLS validators; i.e. 256 epochs after the fork those validators could attempt to finalize a conflicting checkpoint before the fork and avoid being slashed.

Exiting validators via the queue will clog the queue and in case if < 2/3 switched to PQ the network will lose finality and start experience inactivity penalties. Compromising the length of WS period around the fork can be mitigated by announcing that explicitly and asking to carefully select the checkpoint when checkpoint-syncing right after the fork.
